chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:
Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: “There is no cutting off [of the hand] for feathers,” meaning all birds.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام, the source of the ruling
key_terms.رِيشٍ: Feathers; here referring to birds as clarified in the report
key_terms.كُلَّهُ: All of it; indicating general inclusion of all birds
key_terms.لَا قَطْعَ: There is no amputation; the hadd punishment does not apply

ai.seo_question: Does stealing birds or feathers require the hadd punishment of hand amputation in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a legal ruling from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام that theft involving feathers, meaning birds generally, does not incur the hadd punishment of hand amputation. Its significance lies in defining limits for the application of the theft penalty within fiqh.
